options: The process of deleting duplicate records from a dataset
The process of compressing a dataset for long-term archiving
The process of creating and maintaining multiple copies of the same dataset in different locations or systems
The process of translating data between formats
The process of encrypting a dataset before sharing it
questions.explanation: Data Replication is the process of creating and maintaining multiple copies of the same dataset in different locations or systems.

questions.stem: What are the goals of Data Replication?
options: To reduce storage costs and remove old data
To anonymise data and satisfy regulators
To standardise data formats across vendors
To limit access to a single authoritative copy
To ensure data availability, improve fault tolerance and enhance performance
questions.explanation: The goal of replication is to ensure data availability, improve fault tolerance and enhance performance by distributing data across storage locations.

questions.stem: How can replicated copies of data be kept consistent?
options: By synchronising them in real time or at scheduled intervals
By never allowing any copy to change
By deleting all but one copy each night
By storing every copy on the same server
By converting them to read-only PDF files
questions.explanation: Replicated data can be synchronised in real time or at scheduled intervals to keep the copies consistent.

questions.stem: In the group project example of Data Replication, what is the first step?
options: Everyone edits a single shared document on one computer
You create the document with the project details on your computer as the initial copy
The group agrees a synchronisation schedule
Each member deletes their old copies
The document is uploaded to a backup tape
questions.explanation: The first step is creating the initial copy: a document with the project details on your own computer, which is then replicated to each group member.

questions.stem: In the group project example, what does Synchronisation involve?
options: Choosing one member's copy and discarding all others
Locking the document so no one can edit it
Printing every copy for comparison
Everyone sharing their updates so each person gets the latest version and all copies are consistent
Merging the document with unrelated files
questions.explanation: Periodically, or when major changes occur, everyone shares their updates and each person gets the latest version, ensuring all copies reflect the most recent changes.

questions.stem: How does the group project example illustrate Data Availability?
options: Each group member has their own copy, so the document is available even if one person's computer is unavailable
The document is available only when the group leader is online
Availability depends on a single shared server
The document becomes available only after the project ends
Availability is guaranteed by printing the document
questions.explanation: Because each member has their own copy, the document stays available even if one person's computer is unavailable.

questions.stem: How does Data Replication provide Fault Tolerance?
options: By validating every record before it is saved
By preventing any user from making changes
By storing data in a compressed format
If one copy is accidentally deleted or corrupted, other copies still exist, reducing the risk of data loss
By running all queries on a single node
questions.explanation: If one copy is accidentally deleted or becomes corrupted, the other copies remain, which reduces the risk of data loss.

questions.stem: How does Data Replication improve performance?
options: By reducing the size of each copy
Multiple copies can be accessed simultaneously, reducing the load on a single source
By forcing all requests through one server
By caching data only in memory
By archiving rarely used data
questions.explanation: Multiple copies can be accessed at the same time, improving performance and reducing the load on a single source.

questions.stem: What real-world analogy is used to explain Data Replication?
options: Keeping a diary in a locked drawer
Paying for a subscription every month
Building a fence around a garden
Storing valuables in a single bank vault
Giving copies of a house key to different family members so each can enter, even if one loses their key
questions.explanation: Data replication is compared to giving copies of your house key to family members: each can access the house independently, and if one loses a key the others still have theirs.

questions.stem: Where is Data Replication described as a common practice in the digital world?
options: In printed archives and libraries
In social media marketing
In databases, storage systems and distributed computing environments
In payroll processing only
In network cabling design
questions.explanation: Data replication is a common practice in databases, storage systems and distributed computing environments to enhance availability, resilience and performance.
